newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen weaker in wake of LIFFE fall.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen weaker in wake of LIFFE fall.

text.p: Japanese government bond (JGB) futures are expected to be weaker during Tokyo trade on Wednesday, with a downside test likely in the wake of a slump during overnight London trade, traders said.

The key September contract slipped to 124.58 on LIFFE against a Tuesday Tokyo close of 124.75 on pressure from strong Japan May industrial production figures, released Tuesday, and the dollar's surge above 115 yen, they added.
While the impact of the industrial production data is unlikely to be significant in Tokyo today, the market will closely watch the dollar's moves against the yen.
Traders said they expected futures to start Tokyo trade weak, with one focus being how far they are likely to fall before investor bargain-hunting kicks in.

One trust bank trader said he expected support to emerge near 124.45, but a trader with a securities firm said that potential weakness in cash bonds could further undermine futures' strength and take the key contract even lower.

The market will closely watch a news conference by Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita at 0600 GMT, with trade possibly becoming sluggish as operators decide to sideline themselves, the trust bank trader said.
